sections.title: Tokens, Context, and Sampling
sections.scope: Tokenization and why filters and tokenizers disagree; context windows and long-context dilution; logits, temperature, top-p/top-k; why outputs are non-deterministic even at temperature 0 on hosted APIs.

sections.title: How Models Learn Behavior
sections.scope: Pre-training, instruction tuning, preference training (RLHF, DPO, RLAIF/Constitutional AI), reasoning-model RL; safety behavior as a learned statistical preference; fine-tuning can remove safety; what providers vs. application builders control.

sections.title: The Instruction Hierarchy and the Single-Channel Problem
sections.scope: Roles (system/developer, user, tool, retrieved content); the hierarchy is trained, not enforced; instructions and data share one token stream with no privileged channel; the root cause of prompt injection.

sections.title: Tools, Agents, Memory, and Retrieval
sections.scope: How tool/function calling actually works (model emits a request, the application executes it); agent loops; memory (short-term context, summaries, long-term stores); RAG and embeddings mechanics; MCP at a mechanical level.

sections.title: Anatomy of a Production AI System
sections.scope: Gateway, orchestrator/harness, model, retrieval, tools, memory, control plane, logging; common patterns (chat, RAG, agent, multi-model); provider-side vs. application-side controls; where guardrails can attach.

sections.title: Safety, Security, and Containment
sections.scope: The organizing framework of the program: safety (the model misbehaves without an adversary), security (an adversary gains or abuses authority), containment (cause-agnostic: limit, observe, stop). Reliability as a sub-class of safety. Mechanism vs. impact classification (a jailbreak is a security mechanism with a safety impact). The control-strength ladder: model < prompt < runtime ML < deterministic architecture < human/operational.

sections.title: Principals, Authority, and Trust Boundaries
sections.scope: Enumerating principals (operator, developer, end user, tenant, tool, retrieved content, other agents, the model itself); assigning authority; drawing trust boundaries across the data flow, including tool results flowing back into context and model output flowing to downstream systems.

sections.title: The Failure Mode Catalog
sections.scope: Catalog of failure modes classified as safety / security / containment with mechanism, example, and real incident: hallucination, harmful content, over-refusal, sycophancy, off-scope behavior, direct and indirect prompt injection, jailbreaking, data leakage, improper output handling, excessive agency, unbounded consumption, supply-chain compromise, memory poisoning, cascading agent failures.

sections.title: Threat Frameworks and Standards
sections.scope: OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications (2025) and OWASP agentic security guidance, MITRE ATLAS, NIST AI RMF and NIST AI 600-1, STRIDE applied to LLM systems; mapping the catalog to them; date-stamp every version.

sections.title: Assume Compromise: Blast-Radius Analysis
sections.scope: The central design test: if the model were fully compromised or misaligned, what is the worst it could do? The insider-risk model (treat the model like a privileged insider). The lethal trifecta (private data + untrusted content + exfiltration channel). Reducing blast radius vs. reducing likelihood.

sections.title: Risk Scoring and Threat Model Documents
sections.scope: Likelihood x impact scoring that depends on the use case; prioritization; documenting a threat model (template); risk acceptance and who signs it; keeping threat models alive as the system changes.

sections.title: Prompt Injection
sections.scope: Direct, indirect, and multimodal injection; why it is unsolved (no parameterized-query equivalent); why detection is a mitigation not a fix; adaptive attacks against detectors; injection vs. jailbreak.

sections.title: Architectural Defenses Against Injection
sections.scope: Designs that bound what injected content can do: privilege separation, dual-LLM (privileged/quarantined), plan-then-execute, CaMeL-style capability/data-flow control, taint tracking, breaking the lethal trifecta, spotlighting/data marking.

sections.title: Input Handling
sections.scope: Normalization (Unicode NFKC, zero-width and homoglyph handling, decoding layers); size and rate limits keyed correctly (pre-auth vs. post-auth); delimiters with escaping or randomized boundaries; injection detection as one layer; defensive system prompts and their limits; never put secrets in prompts.

sections.title: Output Handling and Egress Control
sections.scope: Treat model output as untrusted input to downstream systems: XSS, SQL/command injection, SSRF via model-chosen URLs; data exfiltration via markdown images and links; URL allowlists and egress proxies; content security policy.

sections.title: Data Protection and Isolation
sections.scope: Retrieval-time authorization (filter at query time by the caller's identity); multi-tenant and session isolation; PII detection (regex with validation, NER, purpose-built detectors) and redaction/masking/tokenization; keyed hashing (HMAC) for pseudonymization; data minimization; privacy-preserving logging; memory stores.

sections.title: Identity and Delegation
sections.scope: Agents acting on behalf of users; OAuth scopes and short-lived, audience-bound tokens; no token passthrough; the confused-deputy problem; per-user vs. service credentials; authorization enforced by the tool backend, never by the model.

sections.title: AI Supply Chain Security
sections.scope: Third-party models and weights (provenance, serialization risks), poisoned datasets and RAG corpora, MCP servers and tool-description poisoning, rug-pull tool updates, extensions and plugins; pinning, review, and allowlisting.

sections.title: Content Policy as a Specification
sections.scope: Writing policy that engineers can implement and test: harm taxonomy, allowed/disallowed/needs-care tiers, worked examples and edge cases, context-dependence (same text, different deployments); policy versioning.

sections.title: Detection and Classification
sections.scope: Rules, ML classifiers, embedding similarity, LLM-as-judge; calibration and threshold choice; layered pipelines that route only ambiguous cases to expensive checks; judges are themselves injectable; integration points (SDK, proxy, gateway) and build vs. buy by tool category.

sections.title: Groundedness and Hallucination
sections.scope: Why hallucination is structural; grounding in retrieved sources; claim extraction and NLI/judge-based support checks and their limits (chunking, input limits); citation verification; abstention and 'I don't know' design; high-stakes domains.

sections.title: Over-Refusal and Refusal Design
sections.scope: Over-refusal as a measured failure mode; false-positive cost; designing helpful refusals that do not leak internals; safe completion and redirection; escalation to humans.

sections.title: Sycophancy, Manipulation, and Vulnerable Users
sections.scope: Sycophancy and agreement bias; emotional reliance and companion-style risk; detecting crisis signals and routing to resources; minors; high-stakes advice (medical, legal, financial); persuasion and manipulation risks.

sections.title: Structured Output Enforcement
sections.scope: Schemas (JSON Schema, strict models that forbid extra fields and fail closed on required fields); constrained decoding vs. post-hoc validation and the failure cases of each (truncation, refusals); bounded retries; template-based generation with output encoding.

sections.title: Streaming, Latency, and Failure Behavior
sections.scope: Guardrails on streamed output (buffering windows, retraction); running checks in parallel with generation; latency and cost budgets; timeouts; fail-open vs. fail-closed decisions by risk; graceful degradation and circuit breakers.

sections.title: Least Privilege for Agents
sections.scope: The insider-risk model applied: minimal tool sets per task, read vs. write separation, enforcing parameter constraints in the tool backend (e.g. read-only database roles, exact-match recipient allowlists), dynamic scoping per session.

sections.title: Sandboxing and Egress Isolation
sections.scope: Isolation strength: process, container, gVisor-style kernels, microVMs (Firecracker); filesystem and network isolation; default-deny egress; secrets never mounted into sandboxes; sandbox escape as a realistic threat.

sections.title: Action Gating and Human Approval
sections.scope: Risk tiers for actions; reversibility as a design criterion; approval workflows that show the actual action and data (not the model's self-description); approval fatigue; dry-run and staged execution; compensating actions.

sections.title: Budgets and Resource Limits
sections.scope: Step, token, cost, time, and rate budgets; loop detection; unbounded consumption and denial-of-wallet; per-tenant quotas; enforcing limits outside the model.

sections.title: The Emergency Brake
sections.scope: Human-operated pause, stop, and kill for running agents: who is authorized; what pause means mid-task (checkpointing, in-flight actions); safe-state and rollback; credential revocation as a kill; the brake must sit outside the model's reach and be tamper-resistant; drills. Reference Satya Nadella's 2026 'Models as Insider Risks' essay as context.

sections.title: External Control Plane and Tamper-Proof Audit
sections.scope: Separating the model from the harness and action space; reference-monitor principle (the program must not bypass the mechanism enforcing its permissions); tamper-evident, append-only audit logs the model cannot write to; reproducing outcomes without relying on the model's self-report; no model verifies its own work.

sections.title: Multi-Agent Systems, Memory, and Monitoring
sections.scope: Trust between agents; memory poisoning and what never to store; long-running autonomy; chain-of-thought monitoring and its unfaithfulness; behavioral anomaly detection; containment as model capability grows.

sections.title: Designing Evaluations
sections.scope: Benign and adversarial evaluation sets; labeling guidelines and inter-annotator agreement; representative traffic; contamination; tagging synthetic probes so they do not pollute production metrics.

sections.title: Metrics and Statistics
sections.scope: Confusion matrix, precision, recall, F1, FPR, FNR, attack success rate (ASR) with multiple trials; base rates and why precision collapses for rare events; confidence intervals and sample sizes; ROC/PR curves and threshold selection; latency percentiles; cost per evaluation.

sections.title: Validating Judges and Classifiers
sections.scope: Measuring LLM-judge agreement with human labels; judge bias (position, verbosity, self-preference); adversarial robustness of judges; drift; never letting a model grade its own outputs.

sections.title: Red Team Engagements
sections.scope: Planning, scope and rules of engagement; manual and automated attacks (GCG-style suffixes, PAIR/TAP, many-shot, Crescendo, encoding, low-resource languages); tools by category with examples (garak, PyRIT, promptfoo); judging success; exploitability and severity rating; reporting; coordinated disclosure to vendors.

sections.title: Red Teaming Agents and Multimodal Systems
sections.scope: Testing tool-using agents (AgentDojo-style environments), indirect injection via documents, web pages, images, and audio; measuring harmful actions rather than harmful text; testing the brake and approval flows.

sections.title: Regression Testing and CI
sections.scope: Unit tests for guardrail components that can actually fail; integration tests for pipelines (mock stages to verify ordering); regression suites from incidents; tiered CI (fast on every commit, full suites nightly); performance testing with warm-up and proper percentile computation.

sections.title: Monitoring and Alerting
sections.scope: Operational metrics (block rate, bypass signals, refusal rate, latency, errors, cost); relative-change alerting and alert fatigue; governed, access-controlled sample stores for review; dashboards for different audiences.

sections.title: Incident Response and Disclosure
sections.scope: AI incident severity; containment options for an active bypass (emergency rules, stricter thresholds, disabling a tool or feature, routing to humans, the brake); forensics from audit logs; post-incident regression tests; disclosure to affected parties and coordinated industry sharing.

sections.title: Change Management
sections.scope: Guardrail configuration as code; re-validating on every model, prompt, or policy change; canary and shadow releases with relative thresholds and detection probes; versioning and rollback; guardrail debt.

sections.title: Release Gates and Documentation
sections.scope: Go/no-go criteria for AI releases; system cards; risk acceptance records and ownership; who holds the authority to stop a launch or a running system.

sections.title: Regulation and Standards
sections.scope: Mapping engineering controls to the EU AI Act, NIST AI RMF, ISO/IEC 42001, and sector rules; what evidence auditors ask for; privacy law basics relevant to guardrails (GDPR lawful bases, CCPA/CPRA); date-stamp all regulatory references.
